page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.i2ne.4xlarge is an x86_64 cloud instance hosted on the KVM hypervisor. It is powered by a 2.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8163 processor with 8 physical cores and 16 virtual vCPUs, supported by 33 MB of L3 cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache per core, and 32 KB L1d cache. The processor features hardware support for AVX, AVX-512 foundation instructions, AES cryptography, and FMA bit manipulation. The instance includes 128 GB of system memory, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU, coupled with 3839 GB of attached local SSD storage and a baseline network throughput of 5 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations show balanced multi-core processing performance alongside limited single-core throughput. In multi-threaded workloads, the instance recorded a Passmark CPU score of 13039.61, a multi-core Geekbench score of 5855.0, and a multi-core stress-ng score of 11742.55. In-memory data handling demonstrated 11.7 million Redis SET operations per second and static web serving throughput of 7.76 GB/sec. Large uncached memory reads achieved 66.14 GB/sec bandwidth. Conversely, single-threaded metrics reflect legacy processor constraints, with single-core Geekbench scoring 946.0 and single-threaded gzip compression registering at 19.02 GB/sec. Small 135M model LLM prompt processing reached 810.23 tokens per second, but 7B model prompt processing dropped to 20.14 tokens per second.

The hardware configuration provides high storage and memory density relative to compute allocation. Combining 3839 GB of local SSD capacity with 128 GB of RAM enables high operational efficiency for I/O-heavy workloads that do not depend heavily on high single-thread clock speeds. Recommended applications include relational database deployments, Redis key-value caching, search engines, log analytics, and software compilation tasks.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.i2ne.4xlarge is a local storage-optimized virtual instance equipped with 16 vCPUs (8 physical cores) running on an Intel Xeon 8163 processor at 2.5 GHz, paired with 128 GB of system RAM and 3839 GB of local SSD storage. Designed with an 8:1 RAM-to-vCPU ratio and high local storage capacity, the instance targets data-intensive systems requiring direct-attached fast disk space. Benchmark results indicate moderate multi-threaded performance, with Passmark CPU scoring 13039.61 and multi-core stress-ng achieving 11742.55, alongside 11.7 million Redis SET operations per second. However, single-core CPU throughput remains in lower performance tiers, showing lower speeds in single-threaded gzip compression and text processing. Network throughput provides a baseline bandwidth of 5 Gbps. The high density of local storage and memory makes this instance cost-efficient for self-hosted databases, caching layers, and search index nodes where local disk I/O performance outweighs individual core execution speed.
